# Sources & Handoff — the-board-on-the-wall

Everything the draft rests on, with citations, plus the council record and the pre-publish
checklist. Written so the author can edit the draft directly without losing provenance.

> **Demo piece — FICTIONAL.** Kestrel Bay Ferry Authority, Terminal 4, its people, and every
> detail below are invented for this repo. The speaker clearances recorded here are part of the
> fiction — they are shown in the shape a real piece's checklist takes, because that shape is part
> of what this voice pack requires. There are no external citations anywhere in this repo.

## Provenance (every detail in the draft traces here)
This piece has no documents, no figures, and no external sources. Its evidence pool is
`transcript.md`, and per `voice/demo-mira/voice-guide.md` nothing appears in the draft that a
speaker did not say. The table below is the whole audit.

| Detail in draft.html | Source in transcript.md | Cleared? |
|---|---|---|
| Magnets warm from the window; board on the back wall of Terminal 4 | narrative-prober Q1 | yes |
| "Two boats, three crews, one that's always in the yard" | stakes-prober Q1 (quoted by the scheduler on the 06:40) | yes |
| Blue / red / white magnet meanings | layperson Q1 | yes |
| The chipped red magnet, "since about 1998" | stakes-prober Q4 | yes — approximate date kept as spoken |
| Only the duty superintendent moves a red magnet; "who moved the Cormorant?" | layperson Q3 | yes for the rule; **vessel name is the author's invention** (see checklist 4) |
| The meeting, five people, the unanswered question | narrative-prober Q2, Q3 | yes |
| "A schedule is not a list of sailings; it is an argument about who is where" | stakes-prober Q1 | yes — paraphrase of a spoken line, no quotation marks used |
| People walking to the empty wall for two weeks, including those who asked for the system | narrative-prober Q4 | yes |
| "Fine. But tell me who's allowed to move the red ones." | narrative-prober Q3 | yes — verbatim, speaker reviewed |
| The clerk writing it into the open-items column | stakes-prober Q3 | yes |
| 05:40, deckhand with no login, screen off, empty office | stakes-prober Q2 | yes |
| "Everybody who needed the board could read it from the doorway." | layperson Q4 | yes — verbatim |
| Printed daily sheet on the wall for a month; the yard's status-code problem | stakes-prober Q4 | yes |
| Eleven days slower | stakes-prober Q3 | yes — scope deliberately limited (see editorial NOTE) |
| The brass rail; "I could read it from the door." | layperson Q5 | yes — verbatim, speaker reviewed |

Cut for lack of provenance (recorded so nobody re-adds them):
- A line about the board's paint color, offered by the machine in v1 — no speaker described it.
- A composite "the schedulers felt" paragraph — this voice prohibits composites.
- Two reconstructed sentences attributed to the operations manager — marked
  `[GAP: confirm quote]` in v1, never confirmed, cut in v2 rather than softened.

## Council record

### Round 1 — 2026-09-17 · editors selected: 6
Mandatory: `slop-allergist`, `voice-guardian`, `presentation-reviewer`.
By fit (narrative essay a stranger will land on from a link): `cold-reader`, `closer`,
`idea-density`.
Not loaded: `partner-brand-steward` (no partner configured), `technical-reviewer` (nothing
technical is claimed), `durability-reader` (round 2 only, added to test the ending).

| Editor | Score | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| voice-guardian | 7/10 | Three drifts into demo-dana's register: one "X, not Y" contrast ("It was a room failure, not a system failure" — the guide bans the construction outright), four inline em-dash pairs in a single paragraph, and a bullet-shaped list of magnet colors that read as an outline. Also one adjective doing the work of detail ("bittersweet"). |
| slop-allergist | 8/10 | No hard fails. Two soft tells: "the usual weather" used twice, and a manufactured-profound candidate in the closing paragraph. Neither caps; both flagged. |
| presentation-reviewer | 9/10 | One `<h1>`, clean `<h2>` sections, no skipped levels, no decorative glyphs, `<hr>` used as a scene break rather than `* * *`. Figure captioned in full sentences per the voice guide. |
| cold-reader | 8/10 | A reader who has never worked a terminal follows the board and the colors. Two gaps: "the 06:40" is never glossed as a sailing time, and "duty superintendent" is used before it is explained. |
| closer | 7/10 | v1 ended on a summary sentence restating the legibility argument. Dribbles. The rail paragraph two above it was the stronger landing. |
| idea-density | 8/10 | One idea, clearly: legibility to everyone in a room is a form of access that a permission model does not reproduce. The eleven-days section competed with it for ownership of the piece. |

**Round 1 aggregate: 7.8 / 10** — below the 9 bar. No hard caps in force; the shortfall was
voice drift and a weak landing.

### Editorial fixes applied (v2 → v4)
1. Rewrote the "room failure, not a system failure" contrast into two sentences that show both
   things, per the voice guide's ban on the construction.
2. Split the em-dash paragraph into three sentences; removed the remaining dash pairs
   (content-lessons rule of 2026-08-14).
3. Converted the magnet-color list into prose in scene order — blue, red, white — so the colors
   arrive as the room sees them.
4. Cut "bittersweet." Replaced it with what was sweet and what was bitter: the system was
   correct, and the wall was gone.
5. Cut the summary ending; promoted the rail paragraph and closed on the sentence about the deckhand
   at twenty to six. *(closer)*
6. Glossed "the 06:40" as a sailing and "duty superintendent" as the role, on first use.
   *(cold-reader)*
7. Reduced the eleven-days section to one paragraph and recorded the scope decision in the
   editorial block. *(idea-density)*
8. Cut three unprovenanced details (paint color, composite paragraph, two reconstructed quotes)
   rather than softening them. *(voice-guide: nothing invented)*

### Information gaps routed back to Step 2
1. → `layperson`: "What exactly was on the rail overnight, and who counted it?" — answered
   (layperson Q5), and the answer became the closing section.
2. → `stakes-prober`: "Did the superintendent say anything else about keeping the rail?" —
   answered: he did not, and the piece says so. A negative answer that closes a gap is still a
   closed gap.

### Round 2 — 2026-09-19 · same five editors plus `durability-reader`

| Editor | Score | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| voice-guardian | 9/10 | Register holds throughout: scene before point, present tense only inside scenes, no lists, no code, no contrast construction. One fragment paragraph is sanctioned. |
| slop-allergist | 9/10 | Sanctioned patterns (scene opener, first-person reflection, quoted speech as structure, the repeated image of the board) deliberately not flagged — they are this voice's house style. No universal tells remain. |
| presentation-reviewer | 9/10 | No hard fails. Figure is inline SVG with a sentence caption. |
| cold-reader | 9/10 | Both terms glossed; the piece survives being screenshotted at the rail section. |
| closer | 10/10 | Lands on an image the speaker supplied. Would survive being quoted alone. |
| durability-reader | 9/10 | Evergreen: the argument is about legibility and access, not about a product or a vendor. Half-life verdict: evergreen. No date-bound framing presented as permanent. |

**Round 2 aggregate: 9.2 / 10 — clears the bar.** Stage moved to `ready-for-human-pass`.

## Pre-publish checklist
1. [x] Every detail in the draft traces to `transcript.md` (table above).
2. [x] Every quote is verbatim from the transcript or cut. No composites, no reconstruction.
3. [x] Speakers quoted by role, not by name, per `voice/demo-mira/style-guide.md`; both reviewed
      the paragraphs they appear in and cleared them (fictional clearances, dated 2026-09-18).
4. [x] Invented detail disclosed: the vessel name *Cormorant* is the author's, appears only
      inside a quoted question, and is recorded here rather than passed off as sourced.
5. [x] Numbers labeled as memory where they are memory ("about 1998," "eleven days," "a month").
6. [x] Diagram drawn from a description, and the caption says so — it is not presented as a
      photograph or a document.
7. [x] Editorial block carries no open GAPs. It is removed at the human pass, before any external
      share (`engine/feedback-intake.md` two-versions guardrail).
8. [ ] **Author's pass, not the machine's:** read it once for the sentence-level ear, adapt the
      two excerpts for the social destination, and publish. The machine does not publish.

## After you publish
Come back and run Step 7 (Lessons): the machine diffs your published version against v4, proposes
generalizable lessons, and on your explicit yes appends them to
`voice/demo-mira/content-lessons.md`. Two candidates are already visible in the diff between v1
and v4 — the em-dash rule and the "if the last line could be said about any object in any
workplace, it is not the last line" rule — but they are recorded there, not here, because they
were confirmed during the council rather than against a published version.
